messages:
jess: FYI repro for a noisy OOM on prod-v2. Happens under steady kv-cache warmup + 1k concurrent short requests. Full log attached.

samir: Interesting — I hit a similar spike in staging yesterday. memory used jumps ~1.8x then many tiny frees create fragmentation. suspect interaction of expandable_segments + small max_split_size_mb.

marta: Can you paste the allocator flags you used? I want to reproduce locally.

jess: Here are the env knobs I used for the run that failed:
```
TORCH_ALLOCATOR_KWARGS=\"expandable_segments=true,max_split_size_mb=32,garbage_collection_threshold=0.6\"
REPRO_WORKER_COUNT=64
KV_CACHE_PREFILL=0.7
```
Log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] Alloc 3072MB slab id=14
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] Free 64KB chunk id=14:frag=0.72
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] OOM when allocating 2048MB (available contig=1792MB)
```

liam: That contig < request suggests too much splitting? With max_split_size_mb=32 we end up with many small splits and higher fragmentation. expandable_segments=true will grow but creates small segments that don't coalesce.

marta: Agree. Two ideas: (A) increase max_split_size_mb to reduce split count, (B) enable a slab-recycle policy that favors reusing larger free chunks before splitting.

devx: +1 on slab recycle policy. We have a prototype policy in the allocator test harness: `recycle_policy=largest_first` that prefers larger holes.

samir: Ran quick perf test with synthetic kernel mix. Baseline knobs (32MB split): p50 latency 45ms, OOMs=7/1000, fragmentation 68%.
With max_split_size_mb=128: p50 47ms, OOMs=1/1000, frag 52%.
With recycle_policy=largest_first + split=64: p50 46ms, OOMs=0/1000, frag 38%.

jess: Great numbers. The slight p50 bump is acceptable. But we need to ensure no regression at high-batch lengths — batching heuristics rely on many small buffers.

liam: We should run cross-product: {expandable_segments=true/false} x {max_split_size_mb=32/64/128} x {recycle_policy=none/largest_first} under our bench with kernel selection freq distribution.

marta: I'll spin the matrix tomorrow on a 4-GPU rig and send perf artifacts. Also will capture nvtx ranges and nvprof timeline to identify if kernel selection interacts with allocation bursts.

devx: Suggest adding a lightweight GC pass trigger: when fragmentation > threshold AND free_pool_large_chunks < X, run async garbage collection sweep. Config knobs:
```
garbage_collection_threshold=0.65
async_gc_enabled=true
async_gc_min_large_mb=256
```

samir: Quick note — async GC helps but defers latency spikes to background; we need a hard fallback path to reject large batched requests when contiguous memory insufficient. Otherwise tail p99 explodes.

jess: For rollout plan: 1) bench matrix on staging 2) enable recycle_policy on a small canary 3) observe OOMs and p95/p99 24h 4) if stable, bump max_split_size_mb globally to 64. Can we automate the canary switch in infra? @infra-bot

infra-bot: Received canary request: will schedule canary cluster with tag "slab-recycle-2026-03-18". Default traffic 2% for 6h, alert on OOM_rate > 0.1% or p99_latency increase > 20%.

marta: I'll attach bench results in this thread when ready. Also adding a small script to repro locally:
```
# repro.sh
python bench_alloc.py --workers 64 --kv-warmup 0.7 \
  --allocator "expandable_segments=true,max_split_size_mb=64,garbage_collection_threshold=0.65,recycle_policy=largest_first"
```

liam: Nice. One more thought: track per-slab fragmentation metric in console so we can correlate with model rollouts. Right now we only have global GPU free.

devx: Will add a per-slab metric (percent_free_by_chunk_size) to the runtime exporter. ETA 2 days.

jess: OK, next steps captured. Thanks all :thumbsup:
